outcome: The general congruent number problem remains open: a full unconditional characterization still requires the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, which is unproven. Work since 26 January 2024 consists of restricted non-congruence criteria for special residue classes (variants/cases, not the stated problem), a machine-learning study of arithmetic statistics of congruent-number elliptic curves that classifies rather than proves, and several non-peer-reviewed preprints claiming full BSD proofs that show no sign of expert acceptance.

ai.basis_quote: Machine learning techniques are being employed to ascertain whether a given square-free integer is a congruent number... exploring the efficacy of computational methods in distinguishing congruent from non-congruent numbers based on the arithmetic properties of elliptic curves.

summary: The congruent number problem as stated (determine precisely which rationals are congruent numbers, a corollary of BSD via Tunnell's theorem) is still open, and nothing found since 26 January 2024 changes that. I found four categories of relevant material. (1) Restricted, unconditional non-congruence criteria for special residue classes: a 2024-vintage 'Pythagorician divisors' approach (SCIRP, 'A New Proof for Congruent Number's Problem via Pythagorician Divisors') and subsequent Shimura-lift work by Hourong Qin and collaborators (building on arXiv:2307.07438, with a 2604.xxxx-numbered April 2026 paper 'A necessary condition for a congruent number of the form 8k+3', and a June 2025 extension to curves E_n: y^2 = x^3 + 2n^3, plus a February 2026 ScienceDirect paper on non-congruent numbers via 2-primary Shafarevich-Tate group criteria for 'multiples of non-congruent numbers'). These are all narrower sub-questions (specific residue classes or families) rather than the general problem, and per §3.1 a case/variant of this kind is at most `partial` for the sub-case, not a change to the bullet as stated; none amounts to a general characterization, so I have classified the overall record as `open` rather than manufacturing a `partial` record for a narrow residue-class result, since the triage's own scope reasoning ('recent hits are about special/related cases... rather than the stated problem') is correct and I found nothing that removes territory from the general problem in a way a careful reader of this specific bullet would flag as settling part of it beyond what was already known before 2024 (partial congruence/non-congruence criteria for special forms existed well before the frozen date too). (2) A September 2025 paper (arXiv:2509.03129, 'Unveiling Arithmetic Statistics of Congruent Number Elliptic Curves via Data Science and Machine Learning') that uses a_p Frobenius-trace data as ML features to classify square-free integers as congruent/non-congruent, and separately tests Goldfeld's conjecture empirically on ranks/Selmer groups up to 3 million; the authors themselves frame the ML component as a classification/statistics exercise run alongside, not in place of, rigorous number-theoretic verification, so it produced no proof and is not a case of the problem being settled. Under §6.2 this is `ai_role: none` because the ML model classified/predicted rather than producing mathematics that appears in a proof. (3) Several 2024-2025 preprints claiming a full, unconditional proof of BSD (via an 'İran Formula' on preprints.org, a 'CASU framework' on ResearchGate, 'Relational Field Theory' on SSRN, and others on Zenodo/IJAEMR) which, if genuine, would resolve the congruent number problem outright; these are all self-published on non-peer-reviewed platforms with no expert digestion, no journal acceptance, and no citation uptake, bear the hallmarks of crank mathematics (grandiose acronyms, unconventional venues), and involve no disclosed AI system. They do not meet the bar for `claimed` (no coherent single preprint with any expert engagement) and I have not elevated the record on their basis. (4) 'ThetaEvolve: Test-time Learning on Open Problems' (arXiv:2511.23473), which does use an AI system (Claude) for open-problem exploration, turned out on inspection to be unrelated to the congruent number problem (it covers circle packing and other optimization-style open problems), so it is not relevant here despite surfacing on an AI+open-problems search. Overall: no case, bound, or full resolution changes the stated bullet since 26 January 2024, and no AI system produced mathematics that entered any result on this problem.
competing_reading: One could argue the residue-class non-congruence criteria (8k+3 case, the E_n: y^2=x^3+2n^3 family, the 2-primary Sha criteria for 'multiples of non-congruent numbers') should be recorded as `partial` since they are, strictly, cases of the general problem (they settle congruence-status for specific infinite families of integers). I judged this is not new in kind — this style of restricted criterion (going back decades, including pre-2024 Qin-style Shimura-lift and Tunnell-style refinements) is exactly the sort of narrow-family result the field has produced continuously, and none of it moves the 'precisely characterize all rationals' bullet in a way a careful reader would flag as a discrete event; the safer reading consistent with the triage's own note is `open`/`no_change_found`. If a downstream reviewer prefers strict literalism about §3.1's 'a case counts, normally as partial', the record should instead be `partial`, direction `mixed` (some numbers confirmed non-congruent, others left open), dated to the April 2026 or February 2026 papers, with `ai_role: none` regardless.
what_would_settle_it: Whether the dataset's convention treats routine, continuous incremental non-congruence criteria for narrow residue classes (a genre of paper that predates 2024 by decades) as `partial` events worth a discrete record, or as business-as-usual background noise that does not constitute a change to 'the problem' bullet. A ruling on this would resolve the ambiguity for every open Diophantine-classification problem on the list, not just this one.
